summary.text: In an August 19, 2025 official statement, Bowman said she continued to be encouraged by significant ongoing investments in AI and machine learning and that some initial benefits of bank AI adoption were already visible [s1]. In the same statement, she said changes ideally would occur with regulators' willing embrace so that AI use cases could proliferate in a way that benefits the banking system [s2]. In a November 22, 2024 statement, she said AI use must comply with current laws and regulations, including fair lending, cybersecurity, data privacy, third-party risk management, and copyright [s5], while also saying regulators should preserve banks' ability to innovate and realize AI's benefits [s3]. She also said that while she had suggested regulators need not rush to regulate, it was important to continue monitoring AI developments [s7].
